newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers remain bullish on US debt--MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers remain bullish on US debt--MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers continued to extend the durations of their U.S. debt portfolios in the week ended February 18, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"Money (moved) in several ways," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, adding that cash levels dipped and investors moved further out on the yield curve.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 107.7 percent from 107.1 percent the week before.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
McTeague said that investor appetite may be "tapering off" because the 'Percent Next Likely Move Buy' portion of the survey hit a new low.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 10 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," compared with 25 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 23 percent, up from 16 percent in the week ended February 10.
Sixty-seven percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 59 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.98 percent, against 3.12 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 35 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 32 percent the previous week, while six percent underweighted it. The remaining 59 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 44 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 10 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants, who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
